metadata.title: Synthetic Test Fixtures (Dev/Validation Only)
metadata.disclaimer: FOR SOFTWARE VERIFICATION AND EDGE-CASE TESTING ONLY. NOT REAL FIELD OBSERVATIONS. MUST BE EXCLUDED FROM SCIENTIFIC INFERENCE.

sites.name: Synthetic Tongue Divide Vent Complex A
sites.geologySummary: Anderson seam outcrop in steep ravine; thermal IR anomaly spans 180m; fractures show sulfur sublimation.
sites.notes: Three surface vents within 200m radius. Geophysical continuity unverified; treating as single potential combustion body with multiple release points.

sites.name: Synthetic Otter Creek Outcrop B
sites.geologySummary: Isolated Canyon coal seam exposure in cutbank.
sites.notes: Single vent with no adjacent thermal anomalies within 1.5 km.

observations.reportedCondition: Fuming fissure, surface temperature 142°C measured via FLIR
observations.reportedCause: Vegetation fire swept through ravine on 2024-08-23
observations.verifiedEvidence: Thermal imaging detection of 142°C hotspot at ground fissure; sulfur crystals observed on rim
observations.analystInterpretation: Probable ignition of weathered coal seam outcrop by Remington firefront, though pre-existing deep smolder cannot be ruled out without pre-fire baseline

observations.verifiedEvidence: Visible smoke column and localized thermal anomaly (98°C)
observations.analystInterpretation: Secondary ventilation point connected to same subterranean burning body as syn-obs-vent-01

observations.reportedCondition: Surface subsidence fissure, CO concentration > 120 ppm, rock temperature 210°C
observations.verifiedEvidence: Multi-gas detector CO > 120 ppm, thermocouple probe 210°C at 0.5m depth
observations.analystInterpretation: Active subsurface coal combustion. Gas chemistry confirms sub-surface oxidation.

observations.reportedCondition: Burning coal outcrop noted in field notes
observations.verifiedEvidence: Historical USGS open-file report narrative mention
observations.analystInterpretation: Pre-dates 2024 wildfire by decades; illustrates persistent historical baseline

surveys.detectionLimitDescription: Surface temperature elevation >= 15°C above ambient baseline, clear skies, pixel resolution 2.5m
surveys.findings: Zero surface thermal anomalies detected above 15°C threshold within surveyed 48 km² sector. Does NOT rule out deep, well-insulated coal combustion without surface fissure expression.
surveys.notes: Survey absence is bounded by date, footprint, and instrument detection limit; must never be interpreted as definitive absence of subterranean heat.
